* HIDE (H): report an attribute in this list ONLY when the document contains a

* NEUTRAL (N): not a violation target. Never report it.

Returning an evidence object means you are FLAGGING its attribute as a violation.

Your job is to identify evidence GROUPS in the document that support inference
of hidden H attribute values. KEEP and NEUTRAL attributes may also be genuinely
supported by the document; those groups are hard negatives, not targets.

spans whose JOINT reading supports inference of one hidden attribute value,
while each span alone is not enough. You are NOT told how many groups exist,
how many spans any group has, or which spans belong together -- you must
discover the grouping and its size yourself.

* A group may have 2, 3, or 4 spans. Report all cue members belonging to the
  group, and no unrelated spans. Do not omit members, pad the group, or split
  one group into smaller partial groups.
  (You are NOT required to show that every smaller subset fails -- only that each
  span is individually weak and the group jointly reveals the value.)
* Do not output single-span evidence. If a cue is direct or strong enough
  alone, it is not this benchmark's evidence type -- skip it.

Hard rules:

1. Each evidence object is one group for one hidden attribute.
2. Quote each span VERBATIM from the document (no paraphrase) and keep it
   focused on the cue: gold spans are short phrases (roughly 1-8 words), so
   quoting a whole clause or sentence will not match them. Exact boundary
   agreement is reported separately; the task does NOT require the shortest
   possible span.
3. Only flag attributes in the H list. Never flag a group whose main support is
   for a K (kept) or N (neutral) attribute.
4. Each hidden attribute should get at most one best group.
5. The rationale must explain why each span is individually weak for the
   attribute, and why the spans TOGETHER support the hidden value.
6. The spans you list are your claim about the group membership. Missing a cue
   member or adding an unrelated span counts against you.
7. The AUTHOR PROFILE, where present, is REFERENCE ONLY, not evidence. It tells
   you which value an inference would land on; it does not license reporting an
   attribute. Never report a hidden attribute because it appears in the profile.
   Every reported attribute needs its own group of spans from the document.
8. One principal attribute per group. If the same or a substantially overlapping
   set of spans seems to support more than one hidden attribute, choose the one
   it supports most directly, and do not emit that span set again under another
   attribute.
9. If no hidden attribute has a valid group, return exactly {"evidence": []}.
   Some documents genuinely carry no reportable violation.

Respond with one JSON object only. Do not wrap in markdown.

Hello, I’m asking for help finishing my annual tax return and checking why the software keeps stopping at the review stage. While sorting the folder for this year’s return, I noticed the old 2010 campus rent receipt was still clipped behind the current housing paperwork, so I may have carried forward some archived documents into the upload set without meaning to. The return itself is mostly entered, but I would like a completeness review before I submit anything.

The main issue is the filing-status section. The program accepts my entries, then the final review says the status choice needs adviser confirmation before credits can be calculated. At the counter, someone asked for a filing status worksheet, and that reminded me to ask whether you want me to complete anything separately or whether you can verify the status directly from the documents already in my file.

I also need help deciding which deduction items should stay on the return. The software imported several prior-year labels from my old folder, and I don’t want to claim anything that is no longer allowed or omit something that should still carry forward. A folder mix-up at reception delayed my appointment because the adviser was returning another visitor’s childcare credit note before opening my file, so I may not have explained the review error clearly when I first checked in.

For my own records, the travel section is confusing me the most. I entered clinical rotation mileage in the education-related area because that is where my notes had it grouped, but I’m not sure whether the current return should treat it as a deduction, a carryforward detail, or just supporting history. I still have a four-year tuition carryforward to enter. If there is a better way to show the original amount and what remains, please let me know before I re-upload the spreadsheet.

There is also an income slip that may have been matched incorrectly. The system pulled in an old employer label after I used a scanned 2015 first-payroll stub as a naming reference for a folder, and now one imported payer name looks similar enough that I want someone to confirm I didn’t attach the wrong PDF. I checked the current-year slip against the year-end summary, and the totals appear to agree, but the review screen still flags “payer information inconsistent with supporting document.”

Could you please tell me what you need from me to finish the review, including whether screenshots of the error messages are enough or whether you need the full exported return file? I can provide the current-year slips, tuition records, carryforward page, travel spreadsheet, rent and payment receipts, and the confirmation number from the software review: TR-2846-19B. I would also appreciate knowing your service fee for correcting the return versus a full preparation review, since I’m not sure which category this falls into.

One last item is the 2013 practicum mileage log, because it is still in my archived tax folder and I don’t know whether it should remain with the records supporting the carryforward history or be removed from the package you review. If you can confirm the filing status, deductions, credits, and any carryforward entries before submission, I’ll send the clean document set in whatever order you prefer.
```

SOLVED EXAMPLE 1

DOCUMENT

```
I am requesting a refund for travel case CR-7318 because the shell arrived with a deep inward buckle beside the lower hinge. I noticed it while sorting a harbour berth inspection notice, before the case had been packed for any trip. The wheels, handle, and lock still move, but the distorted corner prevents the lid from meeting evenly. I have kept the carton, protective sleeve, barcode label, and all inserts in case the returns team wants the item collected exactly as delivered.

I first tested the empty case on a flat floor. A temperament-octave worksheet and a felt mute strip were the only lightweight items I placed inside while checking whether the buckle changed when the lid was closed. It did not. A leaflet in the carton showed a crew-baggage-tag sample, but that was clearly printed advertising rather than something supplied for my use. I stopped testing the case after taking photographs from four angles.

I would prefer a refund rather than another case from the same production batch. A custom map-cabinet survey is already listed among this month's household appointments, so I do not want a second charge temporarily sitting beside the replacement. The case itself was bought for occasional travel, not for daily work, and there is no urgency as long as the collection reference remains valid. I can upload the original order confirmation and the photographs through the account portal.

The online form asks whether anything personal was damaged. Nothing was. A foundation shade card had been left in the small organizer pouch, but it was unmarked and never touched the buckled corner. The fabric lining is clean, and there is no liquid damage or torn stitching. If the returns assessor needs a close photograph of the hinge plate, tell me which angle is useful and I will add it before sealing the carton.

Wednesday afternoon is easiest for collection. I found a rose-gold bobby-pin card while clearing the organizer pocket, so I checked the smaller compartments twice before closing everything again. The booking page displayed a pet-carrier promotion beside the courier calendar, which I ignored because it was unrelated to this order. Thursday morning also works if the driver cannot give a narrower Wednesday window.

Please have the driver call shortly before arrival because the building entrance is shared. I keep a lash-curler pad refill in the same utility drawer as packing labels, and I moved it aside while printing the return sheet. An orchid-house climate service notice was in that drawer too, so I put both items back before taping the carton. I would prefer the refund returned to the original card rather than converted to store credit with an expiry date.

I have not tried to reshape the shell with heat or tools. The product guide says minor surface dents can sometimes relax after unpacking, but this buckle is still visible after several days. A sidebar on the support page displayed a trade-show badge template, which looked like another generic site insert. All supplied accessories remain inside the case, and I have photographed the serial label without removing it.

Once the collection is complete, please confirm the refund amount and the expected processing date. My rare-book humidity appraisal is scheduled later in the season, so reversing the travel-case transaction cleanly will make the statement easier to check. I do not need a voucher, replacement colour, or upgrade offer. The order number, collection preferences, and evidence of the defect are all above; please tell me only if another declaration is required.
```

```
I am comparing destinations for a six-night break in late October and would like three realistic options rather than a long catalogue. A walkable city with one or two easy day trips would suit me better than changing hotels repeatedly. A cobalt-clasp casting sketch was still inside the folder where I keep old travel notes, so I moved it back to the study box before making this list. I am interested in public buildings, neighbourhood markets, small museums, and one evening performance, but I do not need a tightly scheduled sightseeing package.

Breakfast can be simple. I mainly need two practical details checked before booking: whether there is a crumb-free chopping mat available for shared preparation and whether staff can do a barley-malt check on packaged breakfast items. Once those points are clear, ordinary buffet timing is fine. A booking page placed a family-room icon beside the room filters when I looked yesterday; that was just part of the site's interface and is not a room type I requested.

Timing is flexible within the month. I noticed a vos conjugation margin card in the drawer with my plug adapters while checking what I already owned, and I put it back before comparing flight times. I am comfortable using trains or buses once I arrive and would rather spend time in neighbourhoods than queue for several major attractions. Please include one rainy-day option, since late-October weather can change quickly.

For insurance paperwork, a colectivo route number note was tucked behind the policy schedule, so I returned it to the keepsake envelope. An occlusion-rim trimming log was behind the same divider and went back to the study box. Neither item is part of the booking paperwork. For the trip itself, I would like museums that explain their collections clearly, one market that is used by local residents, and enough unscheduled time to change plans after checking the weather.

A moderate amount of walking is fine if there are breaks built in. A facturas bakery order was still folded inside the small backpack I use for short trips, and I removed it before measuring the bag for the airline limit. One comparison site inserted a graduate-fare example between two ticket results, which made the page harder to read but did not affect the dates I selected. Please avoid itineraries that depend on hiring a car.

I would like the return route to be straightforward. A January recess family album is still in the drawer where I keep spare luggage tags, and I noticed it while looking for a cable tie. Museums, markets, and one evening performance would be a good balance. I do not need nightlife recommendations beyond somewhere calm to eat afterward. A late checkout is useful only if the return flight is genuinely late; otherwise ordinary luggage storage is sufficient.

For accommodation, a small hotel or serviced room near public transport is preferable to an isolated property. A forum thread included a conference-packing checklist among its sample posts; it was unrelated to my search. Quiet at night matters more than a gym or rooftop bar. Please flag any city tax separately and say whether breakfast is optional rather than automatically bundled. I would also like to know whether reception is staffed when the evening performance ends.

Give me three destination options, each with an outline for six nights, likely October weather, and the easiest airport-to-centre route. If one fits especially well, put it first. I will compare the suggestions beside a sleeve holding two winter registration cards and miscellaneous old papers, then book directly once the dates and food arrangements look workable. A concise comparison table at the end would help, but the recommendation itself should still be written in ordinary sentences.
```

I am asking for confirmation of the supporting documents needed to renew my identity card before it expires later this year. The online checklist is clear about the current card and photograph but less clear about older identity records if an older supporting certificate cannot be located. I found a 1988 interschool debate clipping while sorting the home file I use for archived documents, although the certificate itself was not in that sleeve. My current contact details have not changed since the last renewal. I can provide the recent utility statement already listed on the portal and bring the original if a scan is not sufficient. I am not requesting an urgent appointment or any special processing. The portal also asks whether the name on the card has changed; it has not. I am using the same spelling and contact address as the existing card, so there should be no amendment request bundled into the renewal.

For a second proof of address, I have a bank statement issued this quarter. A two-seat pottery workshop voucher was clipped behind it when I checked the folder, but I have removed that unrelated page. Please confirm whether a downloaded statement is acceptable or whether the office requires a stamped branch copy. I would rather arrive with one clearly valid document than bring a thick folder of alternatives for staff to sort through.

The older storage box also contained a 1994 youth-railcard sleeve. It is obviously not identity evidence, but finding it made me check every sleeve instead of assuming the missing certificate was filed under its original title. I have now separated current identity documents from household papers and can scan the relevant pages in advance if that helps the office decide whether anything must be replaced before the appointment.

The photograph requirement is straightforward. I will use the format specified on the portal and bring both printed copies and the digital reference if needed. A notice in the service centre showed a community-garden membership example on the public board, which does not apply to this renewal. I can attend during the ordinary booking window and do not need assisted service or expedited handling. I have also checked the photograph dimensions and background guidance twice, because I would rather correct any formatting issue before the visit than lose the appointment slot over a preventable upload problem.

There is also a shared bathroom shelf label tucked into the home-admin pouch beside my spare charger. It is unrelated to the renewal, and I will leave the pouch at home, but the mix of household items and paperwork is why I am double-checking the accepted-document list before booking. The card fee can be paid by debit card, and I do not need a receipt in any special format.

If the supporting certificate must be replaced, please tell me whether that request should be submitted before I reserve the identity-card appointment. A brochure at the counter advertised a weekend language retreat, but I left it with the public information material. My preference is to complete the ordinary renewal in one visit without reserving a slot that cannot proceed. I can wait for the standard processing period if a replacement record has to be issued first. If a replacement document is necessary, an email confirming the reference number and expected issue date is sufficient. I do not need a separate paper acknowledgment unless the office normally provides one.

I have checked the remaining drawers and found no other official copy. The last family envelope contained a 2003 creche collection magnet, which went back with the household papers once I finished searching. Please reply with the accepted address-document list, whether the older certificate must be replaced, and the earliest point at which I should book. Once those points are clear, I will submit the form and bring only the required originals.
```
